claims.promise: The user saves an observing location and equipment profile, so a later plan uses their horizon, focal-length and tracking assumptions instead of a generic sky view.

evidence.finding: Inferred from the measured shelf's separate photo planner, star map and satellite tracker products: a saved local context is required to turn their separate outputs into a repeatable trip decision.

claims.deferredReason: No local scout/profile repository or location picker exists; this resolves when a recreated activity preserves a scout and a changed focal length changes its exposure recommendation.

claims.promise: The app composes one chronological plan with darkness and moon windows, named deep-sky target altitude and azimuth curves, planetary and satellite passes, weather and target-specific tracked or untracked exposure guidance.

comparison.limitation: The measured Play listing establishes a high-price photo-planning incumbent, while this proposal's unified astronomy-session sequence is a conversion hypothesis that requires a feature-by-feature market test.

evidence.finding: Five hand-classified astro shelves returned 141 on-job cards of 149 visible cards, while PhotoPills was measured at 4.8 stars, 8,220 displayed reviews, 100K+ installs and a 10.99-dollar paid listing.

claims.deferredReason: The ephemeris engine, altitude solver, SGP4 propagation, weather client and ordered plan renderer do not exist; this resolves when fixed time/location fixtures yield a plan with every constituent window and recommendation.

claims.promise: The user exports the selected session as a compact plain-language brief through Android Sharesheet, including location, time zone, targets, conditions, moon constraints, pass warnings and exposure assumptions.

comparison.limitation: Its sampled critical reviews include a report that 29 plans on a phone could not be easily transferred and another report about a purchased Location Explorer feature, so portable handoff and local clarity are a testable wedge.

evidence.finding: The complaint scan sampled 2 critical reviews from Planit Pro, including the verbatim start "I have just discovered that the 29 plans that I have on my cellphone can't be easi".

claims.deferredReason: No brief formatter or share intent exists; this resolves when an ACTION_SEND test contains the selected session's planning fields.

claims.promise: The user schedules a local reminder before a chosen dark or target-visible window, so a narrow opportunity remains actionable after planning ends.

evidence.finding: Inferred from the measured satellite shelf's time-sensitive passes and the job's named visibility windows; the useful outcome occurs at a future time, not while the planning screen is open.

claims.deferredReason: No notification channel or scheduled work exists; this resolves when WorkManager schedules a notification containing the selected target and time.
